title: Introducing Claude Meetings
format_note: Product story told as a team video call that moves to a shared whiteboard, chat and a notes document, with Claude acting as a participant.
one_thing: Claude joins a team call as a participant and, from spoken requests, builds and sorts the whiteboard and writes the next-steps plan before the meeting ends.

transcript.voice_style: Casual overlapping office greetings from six teammates, then one short spoken request to Claude; the caption track shows no speech after 14 s.
transcript.script_shape: Greetings, a spoken request, Claude's typed replies; a second request at 26 s; a chat thread settles the pie choice; a Sync/Sort/Work tagline swap and the wordmark close it.

structure.frame0: Black ground, one smiling webcam tile and a call toolbar (Mute, Off, Share, Chat, Settings, red End); more tiles join within 0.4 s (strips/window-01-0s.jpg).
structure.first_3s: Tiles fill to six faces and avatars (f0002.jpg at 2 s) while teammates say good morning; no title, caption or logo until 9.4 s.

beats.what: Video call grid fills with six teammates greeting each other; Claude's tile joins at about 6 s.
Close on Claude's tile: sunrise doodle and the words Hey team.
Cream title card Claude Meetings with a voice bubble: Hey Claude, can you start a whiteboard please? Claude replies in a card.
Claude's tile shows Taking notes... then Starting whiteboard as the blob morphs into a doodle.
Whiteboard with Claude's labelled cursor; Claude joins your call and builds alongside you; stickies from five teammates fill the canvas.
Card: So the work starts before the meeting ends; second voice command asks Claude to sort the notes.
Stickies sort into Easiest, Medium and Hardest columns; teammates add emoji reactions and votes.
Chat thread: Teo declares Huckleberry the winner, Claude adds Berry good choice, You ask Claude to organize next steps, Claude says On it.
Meeting notes document gets a Next steps heading and a Huckleberry Hootenanny launch plan Gantt chart.
Tagline typed by a Claude cursor: Sync, then Sort, then Work at the speed of thought.
Coral star grows, then types the Claude wordmark on cream; held silent.

hero_moment.what: The sorted board in three labelled columns with reaction stickers arriving, the visible result of the spoken sort request.

ending.what: Star grows into the Claude wordmark letter by letter between 59.33 s and 59.75 s, then holds on cream while the audio is silent.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Hard cuts at the call start, then shots of 8-15 s (17.08-25.83, 31.54-39.21, 39.21-47.38, 47.38-62.56) in which the interface keeps changing; median hold 0.83 s; no burst; metrics bursts is empty.

look.ground: Two worlds: near-black call and chat screens, and warm cream canvas with a faint grid for whiteboard, cards and ending; 61% of sampled frames are light.
palette: pastel sticky pink, blue, yellow, green, lilac, peach
deep green (plan chart and pie brand)
look.accent_use: Coral is reserved for Claude: blob, star, name tag, cursor label and the word Claude in the Hey Claude bubble (f0006.jpg).
look.type: High-contrast serif for titles, tagline and the document; clean geometric sans for call, chat and sticky text; heavy grotesque for the board heading and plan title.

title_measurements.text: Work at the speed of thought

look.depth: Flat cards with soft drop shadows (f0006.jpg) and a coral glow around the plan card at 48 s (f0024.jpg); no perspective or 3D.

product_ui.camera_on_ui: Cuts between full-frame call, whiteboard, chat and document; inside a shot the board pans sideways (34-38 s), the chat scrolls up (39-47 s) and the plan card scales from the page to full frame (48 to 50 s).
product_ui.notes: Chat and tile-status text is large (f0021.jpg crop); sticky text, call buttons and Gantt row labels are about 14 px on a 720 px frame, under the 2.6% floor. The UI is invented but one coherent pie-company story.

motion.text_entry: Words fade from grey to ink one at a time; the 9-word command completes in about 0.4 s (strips/window-25-27.792s.jpg); tagline is typed with a caret and a coral Claude name tag.
motion.ui_motion: Stickies drop onto the board with moving name-tagged cursors; the sort slides notes into columns; emoji reactions pop on notes; the coral blob morphs into a doodle; the plan card scales up from the page.
motion.camera: Mostly locked frames; sideways pan on the board (f0019.jpg to f0020.jpg), vertical chat scroll, and one zoom into the plan card.
motion.eases: Reveals look eased-out and settle without bounce; the sun doodle grows over about 1.2 s (strips/window-09-8.209s.jpg). Curves not measured.

transitions.cause: Call to cream title card as the spoken request begins; a command or status line precedes most cuts.
Voice command resolves into sorted columns, the doodle swap or a new sticky layout.
Coral star grows into the wordmark; blob turns into the notes doodle.
Board pan, chat scroll and plan-card zoom reveal more of the same surface.

on_screen_lines.text: Hey Claude, can you start a whiteboard please?
Claude joins your call and builds alongside you
What's our special pie this year?
So the work starts before the meeting ends
Claude, sort these from easiest to hardest to produce.
Looks like we have a winner. Huckleberry it is!
Ok Claude, organize next steps to get this launched by the holidays
Sync at the speed of thought
Sort at the speed of thought
Work at the speed of thought

copy.holds_vs_reading_rule: Titles and tagline hold 2.0-8 s and clear 0.5 s + 0.3 s a word; the 9-word sort command is complete for 1.37 s against 3.2 s required, so it reads as a spoken line.

sound.music: Music throughout (describe tag music 0.856); keyboard_musical 0.782, piano 0.661, synthesizer 0.634, electric_piano 0.48, mallet_percussion 0.357, glockenspiel 0.351; tempo about 130 bpm at beat confidence 0.54.
sound.sfx: Captions mark two [snorts] at 6 s and 14 s and [music] cues; no other effect is evidenced; silence spans 4.64-4.84 s and 13.54-14.27 s.
sound.vo_music_balance: Speech sits only in the first 11 s of the caption track; after 14 s the track shows music only. Balance not measurable.
sound.energy_arc: Sections A 0-14 s, B 14-28 s, C 28-34 s, B 34-41 s, D 41-54 s, E 54-62.6 s; short-term loudness peaks at -13.6 LUFS; film ends in 2.5 s of silence from 60.01 s.
sound.sync_to_picture: Not locked: cuts_on_strong_onset_share 0.083 against chance_share 0.22; strong onsets run 61.4 a minute.

good.observation: One invented story (a pie company choosing a flavour) runs through call, board, chat, document and chart, so each surface reads as the next step of the same work.
good.evidence: f0011.jpg, f0021.jpg, f0025.jpg: Huckleberry named throughout

good.observation: Claude acts as a named participant: own tile, own coral cursor tag, and status lines (Taking notes..., Starting whiteboard, Organizing ideas) that narrate the work without a voiceover.
good.evidence: f0008.jpg, f0009.jpg, f0015.jpg; cursor tags in f0011.jpg

good.observation: Each request is shown as a typed card, then a status tile, then the result; this order gives every cut a visible cause.
The payoff board turns 17 loose stickies into three labelled columns with reactions arriving, so the sort is legible at a glance.
The tagline is typed by Claude's cursor and a highlighted verb swaps Sync, Sort, Work, so the closing line demonstrates the product.
The last concrete deliverable, a dated Gantt plan with owners, is readable at full frame and shows the work reaching a finished artifact.
The ending is quiet: a star grows into the wordmark in 0.4 s and holds 2.8 s on empty cream with the audio silent.

weak.observation: Sticky text, call-widget buttons and Gantt row labels are about 14 px on a 720 px frame, under 2.6% of the short side, so they are unreadable at phone width.
The product name arrives at 9.4 s, 15% into the film; the first 9 s show a generic video call with no caption or logo.
weak.evidence: f0001.jpg to f0005.jpg; title at f0006.jpg

weak.observation: Cuts are not locked to the music, and the final 2.5 s are silent, so the film's loudness sits at -15.4 LUFS.
weak.evidence: metrics.json sound: share 0.083 vs chance 0.22; lufs_integrated -15.4

weak.observation: The sort command is fully on screen for 1.37 s though nine words need 3.2 s to read.

rule_candidates.rule: Put the product name in a two-word serif title at 9-10% of frame height, held at least 3 s, once the premise has been seen, not at frame 0.
rule_candidates.evidence: Claude Meetings at 9.6-12.75 s, 69 px of 720 px (9.58%); frames 0-9 s show the call only.

rule_candidates.rule: Shots of 8-15 s are acceptable when the interface inside them changes at least every 1 s; keep a hold under 3 s only for status tiles.
rule_candidates.evidence: Shots 8.75, 7.67, 8.16 and 15.19 s; median hold 0.83 s; median shot 2.71 s in metrics.json.

rule_candidates.rule: Show each assistant action as three beats in order: a typed request card, a 2-second status tile naming the work, then the result on screen.
rule_candidates.evidence: 9.42, 12.75-17.08 s and 25.83, 29.54-31.54 s repeat request, status tile, result.

rule_candidates.rule: A film built from one continuous interface can use hard cuts for every shot change when each cut swaps a dark world for a cream one and follows an on-screen request; zero dissolves.
rule_candidates.evidence: 12 hard cuts, no dissolves in cuts.json; cuts at 9.42, 25.83, 31.54 s switch ground colour.

rule_candidates.rule: A calm film can replace a cut burst with in-shot density: 10 or more new objects and 4 or more labelled cursors landing within 4 s.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0011.jpg to f0013.jpg (20-24 s): 6 to 15 stickies, 5 name-tagged cursors; bursts empty in metrics.json.

rule_candidates.rule: Hold the true peak at or below -1 dBTP, but check integrated loudness after a silent logo tail; a 2.5 s silence pulls a -13.6 short-term peak down to -15.4 LUFS integrated.
End on a wordmark held at least 2.5 s after it finishes forming, preceded by a tagline of 6 words or fewer held about 2 s.
rule_candidates.evidence: Logo complete 59.75 s, ends 62.56 s (2.8 s); tagline Work at the speed of thought, 6 words.

rule_candidates.rule: Invented UI is acceptable when one story with named people, dates and a brand runs through every screen; reuse the same names and object on at least 4 surfaces.
rule_candidates.evidence: Huckleberry and Teo, June, Vinny recur on tiles, board, chat and Gantt (f0011, f0021, f0025).
